---
title: "Parameterization in BayesIRTplot"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

This article provides details on the parameterization of item response theory (IRT) models fitted in `blavaan`, and explains how those parameters are transformed and used for plotting in `BayesIRTplot`.

IRT models may be fitted under different parameterizations and metrics. To scale the latent response variable, two parameterizations may be used: 1) theta parameterization, in which the residual variance of the latent response variable is fixed to one, 2) delta parameterization, in which the total variance of the latent response variable is fixed to one (Kamata & Bauer, 2008). In addition, different link functions may be used to relate the latent trait to the probability of a correct response, including the probit link, which corresponds to the normal-ogive model, and the logit link, which corresponds to the logistic model.

The current version of `BayesIRTplot` supports unidimensional two-parameter IRT models for binary items. In `blavaan`, these models are fitted using the theta parameterization and a probit link (i.e., the normal-ogive model; Merkle, n.d.). `blavaan` provides posterior draws of item discrimination ($a$) and item threshold ($\tau$) parameters. `BayesIRTplot` applies the following transformations and calculations:

1. Under the normal-ogive model, the probability of a correct response ($p$) is calculated as the probability that the underlying latent response ($Y^*$) exceeds the item threshold ($\tau$):
<div style="margin-top: 0.4em;"></div>
$$
p = P(X = 1 \mid \theta) = P(Y^* > \tau\ \mid \theta) = \Phi(a\theta - \tau),
$$
<div style="margin-top: 0.3em;"></div>
$$
Y^* \mid\ \theta \sim N(a\theta, 1)
$$
where $\theta$ is the latent trait and $\Phi(\cdot)$ denotes the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution.

2. Item discrimination ($a$) is then converted from the probit to the logit metric using 
<div style="margin-top: 0.4em;"></div>
$$
a_{\text{logit}} = 1.702*a_{\text{probit}}
$$ and is reported under the logit metric. 
3. Item information ($i$) is calculated as $$
i = a_{\text{logit}}^2 p(1-p)
$$
4. Item threshold ($\tau$) is not transformed and is reported under the original probit metric. 


<div style="margin-top: 1.5em;"></div>

**References:**

Merkle, E. C. (n.d.). *Ordinal models in blavaan.* blavaan. https://blavaan.org/articles/ordinal.html

Kamata, A., & Bauer, D. J. (2008). A Note on the Relation Between Factor Analytic and Item Response Theory Models. *Structural Equation Modeling, 15*(1), 136–153. https://doi.org/10.1080/10705510701758406
